title: Proactive guardrail engine for dynamic deployment revert triggers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need an automated mechanism that can decide when a model deployment should be reverted (reverted = automated stop + route back to stable variant) based on multiple service-level objectives (service-level objectives include latency, error rate, per-request token cost, and throughput). Existing guards are single-metric and configured as static thresholds; they cause either noisy aborts or late reaction to regressions that impact customers or cloud spend.

Goal: Build a Proactive Guardrail Engine (PGE) that fuses signals across latency, error rate, token-cost-per-request, and throughput into a risk score and emits a revert intent when the score crosses calibrated, cohort-aware bands. The engine should support:
- cohort baselining (by customer, route, model family)
- percentile-based and distribution-aware thresholds (p50/p95/p99 and trimmed means)
- token-cost normalization (adjust decision thresholds by projected token spend delta)
- hysteresis and decay windows to avoid flip-flopping
- experiment/A-B awareness so that canaries and A/B cohorts are evaluated vs their shadow/stable counterparts

Non-goals: This ticket will not include UI polish for the Console. It will deliver a config schema, evaluation engine, rollout integration hooks, and a debug API. Console UX refinements and advanced policy templates will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: A runtime service (pge-service) accepts metric streams and cohort metadata and produces a per-deployment risk score every 30s.
Risk score composition is documented: contributions from latency, errors, throughput, and token-cost with tunable weights.
Automated revert webhook fires only when: risk_score > threshold_for_cohort AND simulated false-positive rate < 2% (based on backtest over last 30 days of historical traffic).
Canary and A/B cohorts are evaluated against matched control cohorts using a two-sided test; divergence must be reported even when below revert threshold.
A debug endpoint returns the last 6 windows of raw signals and intermediate normalized features for any active deployment (for SRE/debugging).
End-to-end integration test: a synthetic regression in the canary (latency spike + token-cost increase) triggers revert in staging within 3 minutes and does not trigger for the stable control cohort.
plan: Design: finalize risk score formula and cohort bucketing (week 1) — design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PGE+design
Prototype: implement offline scorer and backtest using 30d telemetry dump (week 2)
Runtime: implement pge-service with a pull-based adapter to our metrics pipeline and an output webhook to rollout-controller (week 3)
Safety: run shadow mode on <dev> and <beta> for 1 week to calibrate weights and fibrillations (week 4)
Rollout: staged enablement for low-traffic routes, then tiered expansion; enable automatic reverts for non-sensitive tenants only initially (week 5-6)

2025-02-21 Asha Patel: Initial design review done. Agreed to use decaying-window percentiles (IQR + trimmed mean) instead of raw means to limit outlier sensitivity.
2025-02-26 Eng lead (Rafael Ortiz): Prototype passed backtest on 30d data with simulated regressions; false positive estimated at 1.1% with conservative weights. Moving to runtime implementation.
2025-03-02 SLI team: Added token-cost normalization function (token_cost_delta * 1.6 weighting) to account for high-cost prompts — flagged for tuning in shadow run.
